title: Apollo 13 oxygen tank explosion and return
summary: Apollo 13 lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on 11 April 1970 with Jim Lovell, Jack Swigert and Fred Haise. An oxygen tank in the service module exploded on the way to the Moon, damaging the spacecraft. The crew survived and splashed down in the Pacific on 17 April, near the recovery ship USS Iwo Jima.

uncertainty.note: Launch 11 April and splashdown 17 April 1970; the explosion date itself is not stated on the pages opened.

as_recorded.value: On April 11, 1970, Apollo 13 lifted off for the moon
splashed down on April 17, 1970, at 1:07 p.m. EST

importance.justification: Survived in-flight emergency that became a defining episode of spaceflight and emergency problem-solving.

beats.caption: Apollo 13 lifted off for the Moon from Kennedy Space Center on 11 April 1970.
After oxygen tank number two exploded, the damaged spacecraft returned and splashed down in the Pacific on 17 April.
The blast also damaged tank one and left the fuel cells unusable, but the crew was recovered safely by USS Iwo Jima.
